english_draft:
This preview is a historical reconstruction. It uses only the Microsoft FY2026 Q3 press release published on April 29, 2026. It was not written before the target-quarter earnings release. It does not use information released after the cutoff.

Conclusion:
- As of the cutoff, Microsoft did not publish quantitative guidance for the quarter ending June 30, 2026. The press release says management will provide forward-looking guidance on the earnings call.
- The prior quarter shows that cloud and AI were the main growth drivers. Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 40% (39% in constant currency). Microsoft Cloud revenue was $54.5 billion, up 29% (25% constant currency). The AI business surpassed an annual revenue run rate of $37 billion, up 123%.
- The next report should confirm whether these growth rates continued. If they continued, total revenue and operating income may follow the prior quarter's 18% and 20% growth. If Azure decelerated or More Personal Computing declined further, total results may be weaker.

Prior-quarter baseline:
- Revenue was $82.886 billion, up 18% (15% constant currency).
- Operating income was $38.398 billion, up 20% (16% constant currency).
- GAAP net income was $31.778 billion, up 23%. Non-GAAP net income was $31.792 billion, up 20%.
- GAAP diluted EPS was $4.27, up 23%. Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $4.27, up 21%.
- Productivity and Business Processes revenue was $35.0 billion, up 17%.
- Intelligent Cloud revenue was $34.7 billion, up 30%.
- More Personal Computing revenue was $13.2 billion, down 1%.
- Commercial remaining performance obligation was $627 billion, up 99%.

Core questions:
1. Can Azure growth of about 40% continue? The prior quarter showed Azure at 40% GAAP and 39% constant currency. Capacity, enterprise demand, and AI delivery may affect the next quarter.
2. Will the large commercial backlog convert into Microsoft Cloud revenue? The $627 billion RPO grew 99%. Its recognition pace determines cloud revenue.
3. Will the weakness in More Personal Computing continue? Windows OEM and Devices fell 2%; Xbox content and services fell 5%. These declines may offset cloud strength.

Potential positives:
- AI business run rate above $37 billion, up 123%.
- Microsoft Cloud and both commercial segments grew at double-digit rates.
- Commercial RPO almost doubled, giving revenue visibility.

Potential negatives:
- More Personal Computing fell 1%; gaming and Windows OEM/Devices declined.
- Foreign exchange moved growth rates. GAAP was higher than constant currency in the prior quarter; future FX swings may affect comparability.
- OpenAI investment losses were small in the prior quarter, but GAAP comparisons may be affected if that changes.

Verification points:
- Azure and other cloud services growth vs. 40% GAAP and 39% constant currency.
- Microsoft Cloud revenue growth vs. 29% GAAP and 25% constant currency.
- Commercial RPO growth vs. 99%.
- Segment revenue growth: PBP 17%, IC 30%, MPC -1%.
- AI business run rate vs. above $37 billion and 123% growth.
- OpenAI investment impact on GAAP and non-GAAP net income.
- GAAP vs. constant currency gaps.

新闻稿没有下季度量化指引，本稿是否误把上季增速当成指引或共识？
Microsoft Cloud 与 Azure 是否同一口径？若混用，读者会把 40% 与 29% 误作直接比较。
fact_checks: 第一轮核实：来源为微软 FY2026 Q3 新闻稿，发布日期 2026-04-29；所有数字均为截至 2026-03-31 的季度数据，单位百万美元。本稿据此将 target_event_date 2026-07-29 对应为 2026 日历 Q2 / 微软 FY26Q4，并在标题和首段明确，不与 FY26Q3 混淆。
第一轮核实：GAAP 净利 $31,778M +23%，non-GAAP $31,792M +20%；GAAP EPS $4.27 +23%，non-GAAP EPS $4.27 +21%。本稿分别列出增长率，未合并为单一数值。
第一轮核实：Azure and other cloud services +40%（CC +39%）是 Intelligent Cloud 分部内的单项；Microsoft Cloud $54.5B +29%（CC +25%）是跨分部口径；RPO $627B +99%。本稿在各段落保持这些层级。
第二轮互检：仅使用新闻稿事实，无下季量化指引和市场共识；本稿未编造数字、股价或产品利润，也未使用财报后信息。对于新闻稿未提供的 FY26Q4 指引，正文明确写为信息缺口。
第二轮互检：为回答读者疑问，最终稿用“上季基准”表示 FY26Q3，用“下一季/本季”表示 FY26Q4；并在验证点中并列 GAAP 与固定汇率增速，避免口径混淆。
